quiz.question: What does a tuple enforce that a regular array does not?

answers.answer: A tuple only allows string elements
A tuple has a fixed length and a specific type at each position
A tuple automatically sorts its elements
A tuple prevents you from reading its elements

quiz.explanation: A tuple locks down both the number of elements and the type at every index. A regular array can hold any number of items of a single type, but a tuple says exactly how many elements there are and what type each one must be.

quiz.question: Given `const item: [string, number] = ["Widget", 9.99];`, what would happen if you wrote `const item: [string, number] = [9.99, "Widget"];`?

answers.answer: It would work because tuples ignore element order
It would silently swap the values at runtime
TypeScript would report a type error because the types are in the wrong positions
It would work but the types of item[0] and item[1] would be `any`

quiz.explanation: Tuple types are positional. The type [string, number] requires a string at index 0 and a number at index 1. Swapping them causes a compile-time type error because 9.99 is not a string and "Widget" is not a number.
